title: Fideuà
subtitle: Valencian noodle paella with seafood
excerpt: The Valencian alternative to paella: short thin noodles toasted and cooked in a rich fish and shellfish stock in a wide pan until the noodles are dry and slightly crisp at the edges. Served with aioli stirred in at the table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fideuà (from the Valencian fideo, meaning thin noodle) was supposedly invented in the 1930s by a cook on a fishing boat off the coast of Gandía who ran out of rice and substituted pasta. The dish became a specialty of Gandía and spread across the Valencian coast, where it is made in competitions following rules almost as strict as paella. The key technique is the same as paella: the stock must be rich and deeply flavoured (a good fish or shellfish stock is essential), the noodles are first dry-toasted in oil until lightly golden (this gives them a nutty flavour and helps them hold their shape), and the dish must not be stirred once the stock is added. The finished fideuà should have a socarrat (the slightly caramelised crust at the bottom) just like paella.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, shallow pan is essential for the socarrat to form. A large frying pan works well.

content.text: Toast the noodles until golden before adding any liquid: this is the defining technique and gives the dish its characteristic flavour. Use the best fish stock you can find or make; the noodles absorb the stock so the flavour of the stock is the flavour of the dish. Do not stir once the stock goes in.

items.preparation: thin short noodles (fideos or vermicelli broken into 3 cm lengths)

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium heat. Add the noodles and stir constantly for 3 to 4 minutes until they turn golden brown. Remove and set aside. In the same pan, fry the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika, and tinned tomatoes. Cook for 3 minutes until reduced.

Add the hot stock and saffron water. Bring to a boil. Return the toasted noodles and spread into an even layer. Add the squid and nestle the prawns on top. Cook over medium-high heat without stirring for 8 minutes. Do not touch the noodles once the stock is in.

Add the mussels, pushing them into the noodles. Cook for a further 5 to 6 minutes until the mussels have opened and the noodles on the bottom have formed a lightly caramelised crust. Remove from the heat and leave to rest for 3 minutes. Discard any unopened mussels. Serve with lemon wedges and aioli.
